Pakistan committed to implementing Saudi defence pact, Makkah agreement: FO. Pakistan on Thursday said it remained committed “in intent and spirit” to implementing the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (SMDA) with Saudi Arabia and the trilateral Makkah Defence Alliance. Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the statement during his weekly briefing. The statement comes amid renewed tensions in the Middle East, with Yemen’s Houthi rebels carrying out attacks in Saudi Arabia in recent days. A day earlier, a Saudi-led coalition battling Houthis accused the rebels of targeting the holy city of Makkah, sparking outrage across the Muslim world and deepening the conflict roiling the region. However, the Houthis swiftly rejected Riyadh’s report as a “lie” that it shot down a drone from the rebels heading towards Makkah. In response to a question on whether “any mechanism had been devised as to how Pakistan will ensure that recent Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia are thwarted,” the spokesperson said that Pakistan was committed to “implementing” the SDMA and the Makkah pact. “However, when, how, where and what force will be used against what objectives, in which modes and matters [..] — operational confidentiality requires us to be discreet at this stage,” he added. Asked about the diplomatic efforts undertaken by Pakistan to “de-escalate and defuse” the Houthi issue, the spokesperson said, “Pakistan has for a long time [..] shared the perspective that we would like to have peace and stability because this is not only in the interest of Pakistan and Iran, but also the entire region and beyond.” Khan termed the situation in Bab al-Mandeb “exceptionally serious” and went on to call on the Houthis to “stop their activities”. “In this regard, our discussions basically revolve around bringing peace and stability through dialogue and diplomacy and not through coercive measures,” he added. PM Shehbaz to head to US next week for UNGA In his press briefing, the spokesperson also confirmed that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will be leading Pakistan’s delegation at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York next week. Khan said that the premier will be accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and several federal ministers. FO said that in his address at UNGA, PM Shehbaz will “highlight Pakistan’s perspective on regional and global developments, reaffirming the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and restraint and peaceful resolution of issues”. He said the premier is also expected to outline Pakistan’s priorities on sustainable development, climate change, counter-terrorism, Islamophobia, global economic challenges, UN reforms and issues concerning the Global South. He will also draw attention to the situation in India-occupied Kashmir and Palestine, the FO spokesperson said. He added that on the sidelines, PM Shehbaz is scheduled to participate in high-level events and hold bilateral engagements with world leaders and the UN secretary general, where he will highlight “Pakistan’s commitment to multilateralism, the UN Charter, regional peace and international cooperation”. ‘Malicious media campaign’ against Pakistan on Sikh pilgrims The spokesperson was also asked about media reports regarding Pakistani Sikh pilgrims who were stopped at Faisalabad International Airport while travelling to India to perform religious rituals at Gurdwara Sri Hemkund Sahib. In response, he termed it a “malicious media campaign” on India’s part and clarified, “It was reported that the pilgrims were not allowed to board the plane, which is not correct.” “We were not aware that the Indian High Commission had issued these visas, and the visas were not covered under the 1974 bilateral protocol that exists between Pakistan and India,” he said, explaining that protocol’s objective was to facilitate visits to shrines between both countries. Khan said the visas were issued “independently of any coordination”. Noting India’s “exceptionally restrictive visa regime,” the spokesperson said Pakistan was committed to “extending a warm welcome to Sikh pilgrims in Pakistan, including from India”. He also cited the number of visas issued to Sikh pilgrims over various religious occasions, stating that the “numbers speak for themselves”. He noted that Indian Sikh pilgrims had been barred by their country from travelling to Pakistan in 2025. Khan also maintained that Pakistan was ready to welcome Sikh pilgrims through the Kartarpur corridor “as and when India allows them because it has been closed from the Indian side and not Pakistan”. Khan was also asked about India’s participation at the 12th meeting of the Heads of Border Services of the Competent Authorities of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). In this regard, the spokesperson confirmed that India’s chargé d’affaires was present at the summit. “Participation is there, and we hope that participation will continue because the broader objective is peace and security and fighting terrorism, and it is a common challenge for both countries.” On being asked about India’s response to Pakistan and China operationalising a joint mechanism for managing their common border, the FO spokesperson rejected India’s “baseless and illegally untenable assertions” on the development and the Joint Boundary Demarcation Commission. The Joint Boundary Demarcation Commission was established under the Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement of March 2, 1963. According to India’s NDTV , the country’s external affairs ministry had called into question the legality of the commission. “China is not only our neighbour but an all-weather strategic corporate partner. Our ironclad ties have withstood the test of time,” he said. He stressed that the 1963 agreement was “valid”. Khan said that it was a “mockery of international law that India spoke of legality in an attempt to challenge the validity of the border commission”. At this, he said the country should first “carry out its own introspection” over actions in India-occupied Kashmir “instead of advancing fictitious territorial claims”.

Pakistan eyes bigger China swap line, expects US financing decision soon. Pakistan will seek an expansion of its 30 billion yuan swap line with China when the facility expires in 2027, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said, adding he expects a US response on a proposed $10bn exchange stabilisation ​facility within two months. The country remains reliant on external financing to bolster foreign exchange reserves and meet debt repayments, ‌making support from China, Gulf states and multilateral lenders key to maintaining economic stability and investor confidence. Aurangzeb said the entire 30bn yuan swap line from China had been fully drawn, adding that the government had yet to decide how much additional financing it would seek when the facility ​comes up for renewal. “They were open to it, but there is a process which has to be followed,” said ​Aurangzeb, referring to recent meetings with his Chinese counterpart and the country’s central bank governor. “We do ⁠plan to make a formal request at the time of the renewal.” Meanwhile, Aurangzeb said he expected a response within two months ​to Pakistan’s request for a $10bn exchange stabilisation facility from Washington, adding that the government was also in talks with the Export-Import ​Bank of the United States (EXIM) and the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC). EXIM financing could support aircraft purchases from Boeing by Pakistan International Airlines now that the national carrier is privatised, while DFC could help fund a planned $5bn programme to upgrade the country’s oil refineries. Asked whether there were any ​concerns about simultaneously seeking additional support from the US and China, Aurangzeb said it was an “and-and” discussion. “China has been a long-standing strategic partner for us … and we have very good, at the leadership level now, understanding and relationship with the Trump administration,” he said. “We are very fortunate to have this kind of relationship with both important economic and superpowers.” The US Treasury, DFC and EXIM did not immediately reply to a request for comment. Asked about elevated crude oil prices following the latest Middle East conflict, which began in February, Aurangzeb said Pakistan had navigated the initial price spike after US and Israeli strikes on Iran relatively well, but cautioned that the outlook had ​become more uncertain. “If this conflict ​goes into, unfortunately, November or ⁠December, you know, this is something which will be an area of concern for us,” he said, adding prolonged disruption could put at risk the government’s 4pc growth target for the fiscal ​year. Pakistan had secured sufficient oil stocks to cover its needs through September and was well positioned ​for October, he ⁠said, adding an institutionalised mechanism was now reviewing the situation on a daily basis . Planning for November supplies was already under way. Nonetheless, Aurangzeb said the government had no plans to seek additional International Monetary Fund (IMF) financing or emergency support from the Washington-based lender. “As of now, our considered ⁠view is ​that it’s manageable.” An IMF mission is due next week for the fourth ​review of Pakistan’s $7bn programme and the third review of its Resilience and Sustainability Facility. “From our perspective, we are in good stead with the quantitative benchmarks, and ​we are largely compliant with the structural benchmarks,” he said.

UN mission finds grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran with strikes on school, sports centre. A United Nations fact-finding mission on Iran said on Thursday it had reasonable grounds to believe the United States was behind two military strikes on a school and sports facility in Iran in February, and that these constituted war crimes. It also said that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during their deadly crackdown on anti-government protests before the war. The findings in a new report by the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran, to be submitted to the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, examined the US’s conduct during the Iran war that began in February and the Iranian government’s response to nationwide unrest that began in late December. The Iranian and US permanent missions in Geneva did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. US officials have previously said military operations are conducted in accordance with the law of armed conflict, while Iran has consistently rejected allegations of systematic rights violations. Minab school strike The UN experts said they found reasonable grounds to believe US forces were responsible for an attack on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in the city of Minab, where more than 150 people were killed, including around 120 schoolchildren, according to Iranian officials. The indiscriminate attack caused civilian deaths and damage to civilian infrastructure, amounting to a war crime under international law, the mission concluded. According to the report, the US failure to update information in relation to the school, which was adjacent to an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) naval complex, in its targeting databases and to confirm the building was a military objective amounted to more than mere negligence. According to the report, the US relied on intelligence suggesting a senior Iranian military commander was present at the site but failed to adequately verify the information before launching the strike. “Rather, the US directed the strikes at the building of the school while being aware of a substantial risk of striking a civilian object and acting recklessly as regards the possibility that this would happen.” In June, US President Donald Trump said that “nobody” purposefully attacked a girls’ school in Iran in February, citing an investigation into the incident. Reuters first reported that an initial internal US military investigation showed US forces were likely responsible for the fatal strike in Minab in southern Iran. The Pentagon has since elevated the probe, but it has not published any preliminary findings. UN experts said the school was a clearly identifiable civilian object and found no evidence that it was being used for military purposes. The experts reached a similar conclusion over a strike on a sports centre in Lamerd . The report said the attack damaged nearby residential buildings and a school and killed and injured 22 civilians. It concluded that the strike was indiscriminate and therefore constituted a war crime. US Central Command said in a statement in March that US forces did not launch any strikes into the city of Lamerd on that day. Iran abuses The UN mission’s probe found that Iranian authorities carried out a widespread suppression of civilians during protests that erupted in late December last year. Tehran blamed “terrorists and rioters” backed by exiled opponents and foreign foes — the US and Israel. The probe said it could not independently verify the death toll, but that it believed the number of dead and injured was likely far higher than official figures , which say 3,038 people were killed and 25,000 people injured. The government’s response to the protests — including violence, cutting off the internet and the use of the death penalty — marked a significant escalation from previous patterns of suppressing dissent, the report said.

Salman Akram Raja says released after PTI claims detention by Islamabad police. PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja on Thursday said he was “released” after being briefly detained, with his party claiming he was held by Islamabad police. In a post on X at 4:39pm, the PTI claimed that Raja, Latasob Satti and “others were unlawfully abducted” when they were on their way to Kotli Sattian to attend a PTI worker’s funeral. A post on Latasob’s Facebook account said his son Ikhlaq Ahmad Satti was also held. The PTI said they were then transferred to Nilore police station in Islamabad, alleging that “abductions and arrests were ongoing to prevent people from attending the funeral”. In a subsequent post at 5:32pm, Raja said he, Latasob, Ikhlaq and their “several friends were released after being kept in detention for four hours”. “The only objective was to prevent us from attending late Ijaz Satti’s funeral. The fear of the public has stripped the decision-makers of their reason and sense,” the PTI secretary general contended, adding that “human rights have become meaningless”. Latasob, a retired major, also shared a picture on X of him and the PTI leaders, saying they had been released. PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan strongly condemned the alleged detention. “For the last few days, about 700 workers have been arrested,” Gohar claimed, adding that arrest warrants have also been issued against MNAs and MPAs. “This is all illegal. This must end now,” he wrote. Earlier in the day, Raja had addressed a press conference alongside PTI leader Taimur Saleem Jhagra. The PTI has been holding party activities to mobilise supporters for the PTI’s nationwide protest scheduled for September 27, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi touring Punjab this week. During his visit, the KP CM not only alleged he was “ abducted ” by authorities in Lahore and later “thrown” by the roadside, but also claimed a man was sent to kill him. The Punjab government had swiftly refuted the claims of arrest, while the Wazirabad police clarified that the man accused by Afridi was a police constable deployed on security duty for the CM. The Punjab government has imposed a ban on gatherings across the province from September 13 to 17. Earlier this week, district authorities had also issued preventive detention orders against dozens of PTI workers under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order, including 31 in one Punjab notification and a further 14 in Toba Tek Singh. The administrations of the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad had already begun preparations to counter the PTI’s announced march to the capital, including a request for the detention of activists, arranging containers, seeking additional personnel and procuring anti-riot gear. On Wednesday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited various checkpoints in Attock connecting Punjab to KP to review security arrangements.

Markets to close at 9pm as govt reintroduces austerity measures for fuel conservation. The federal government reintroduced austerity measures on Thursday in an effort to conserve fuel amid renewed tensions in the Middle East, setting 9pm as the time for closing markets and reducing fuel provision for official vehicles by 50 per cent for a period of three months. The measures are to be implemented with immediate effect, the Cabinet Division’s notification detailing the government’s directives said. According to the Sept 17 notification, seen by Dawn , businesses and commercial establishments are to close at following timings: Shops, markets, shopping malls and bazaars, as well as departmental, grocery, general and kiryana stores are to close by 9pm Marriage halls, marquees and all other commercial places where festive events are held are to close by 10pm Restaurants, cafés, eateries, and food outlets, as well as standalone fruit and vegetable shops are to close by 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services are exempted from the restriction Pharmacies, medical and medical supplies’ stores, medical laboratories, clinics, hospitals, standalone bakeries, standalone tandoors, standalone milk and dairy shops, fuel and CNG stations, electrical vehicle charging stations, gyms, sports facilities and sports/padel courts, IT companies and call centres are also exempted from any time restrictions. Moreover, just a single dish should be served at all marriage-related functions or events, the notification said. The Cabinet Division also detailed comprehensive instructions for government entities and officials. These include the reduction in fuel provision by 50pc for official vehicles for three months. Vehicles of armed forces, civil armed forces, vehicles in use of law enforcement agencies, those used for essential services and those in use of the Federal Board of Revenue are excluded from this restriction barring those of administrative or non-operational formations of these entities. This measure is also not applicable in the case of development projects, according to the notification. The government has also announced a 5pc reduction in the budget for non-employee related expenditures for FY2026-27, with deduction to be made on a monthly basis. “This measure will also apply in the case of foreign missions and the officers/officials, belonging to any occupational group or service, posted in these missions; however, obligations relating to their rents, educational fees and medical care arrangements will be met,” the notification read, adding that this measure too was not applicable in case of development projects. According to the notification, the government also imposed a complete ban on the purchase of vehicles of all types, with the restriction not applicable to development projects. It also prohibited the purchase of all durable goods, except IT-related equipment and services, while clarifying that the measure would not apply to development projects. It further imposed a three-month ban on foreign visits and travel, including obligatory trips for government officials. The restriction, however, would not apply to scholarships offered by international development partners, or to training and courses arranged through the Economic Affairs Division or under institutional agreements of the Government of Pakistan. According to the notification, Pakistan’s ambassador or high commissioner concerned would represent the country at obligatory and important events during the period. However, in case of “unavoidable visits” all ministers, advisors, ministers of state, special assistants to the premier, parliamentary and government functionaries shall “travel only in economy class”. The government further directed that official meetings will be preferably held through teleconferencing, except intra-city meetings. “No official dinners shall be hosted, except in the case of visiting foreign delegations,” the notification added. The notification also prohibited all government-funded official seminars, trainings and conferences. However, where such events were deemed unavoidable, government facilities, including auditoriums and committee rooms, would be used to host them. It further said requests for exemptions from any of the measures could be considered on a case-by-case basis by the Committee for Monitoring and Implementation of Fuel Conservation and Additional Austerity Measures. The committee would then submit its recommendations to the prime minister for approval. Earlier this week, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that the government was considering reviving austerity measures introduced during a previous fuel conservation drive amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East. The government had earlier imposed austerity measures on March 9 to mitigate the impact of the ongoing US-Iran war . These included a 50 per cent cut in fuel allowances for official vehicles, salary cuts for lawmakers, and a partial work-from-home policy in the public sector. The government ended the measures on June 19, except for market timings. The move comes amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have disrupted major oil supply routes and led to a rise in fuel prices. In addition to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz stemming from the US-Iran war, trade through Bab al-Mandab — which has become a vital route for Saudi oil exports in recent months — is also facing a growing threat from Houthi rebels.

'A chief minister's trips are never personal': Maryam claps back at criticism over use of govt aircraft. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Thursday shot back at criticism over her use of an official aircraft to attend a family event in London, claiming that a chief minister’s trips “are never personal” and insisting she had borne all trip-related expenses. CM Maryam came under scrutiny when it emerged that she used the provincial government jet to make a private visit to London, with opposition leaders questioning the use of an official aircraft for a family event. However, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari has denied the allegation, also insisting that the trip was paid for “out of her own pocket”. Addressing a ceremony in Multan, the chief minister addressed the issue, noting criticism “directed at Maryam Nawaz’s plane”. “It is not Maryam Nawaz’s plane; it is the chief minister’s plane. Maryam Nawaz is not going to take it to Raiwind [..] all four chief ministers have this facility,” she said. She said she had served Punjab for two-and-a-half years. “I wake up, I go to work and come back in the evening [..] sometimes, I am working till so late that I fall asleep with my iPad or phone in my hand”. The chief minister said that if she promised people a project, “Maryam always delivers double of that,” referring to herself in the third person. “If she has committed 1,000 buses, she will give 5,000 [..] but sometimes for these projects, sometimes I have to go places — by cars or by plane [..] was I not on the rescue boats when catastrophic floods hit Punjab in 2025,” she said. Noting that the chief ministers of all four provinces availed the facility, she said, “It is available to everyone, but the criticism is directed only at Maryam Nawaz”. “Today, as I was coming here, I thought since there has been so much criticism, perhaps I should go by Qingqi or motorcycle, or if there is a metro bus I can take till here from Lahore,” she quipped. She then cautioned the audience to be wary that “the criticism is not aimed at me, [but] rather [at] Punjab’s development and growth. It is directed at the mirror we hold to them [other provinces] every day.” CM Maryam said that for the past two and a half years, she had been eager to see other provinces say they were doing better than Punjab. She further held that the “Rs9 billion jet” was not hers, but rather belonged to the office of the chief minister. “Tomorrow, if I go to Sargodha and have to go to Rawalpindi [..] How will I get around?” she questioned, stressing that the “most precious resource for a CM is their time”. She said that she was heavily criticised solely “because I am doing the work and have left the others in a position where they have to save face”. CM Maryam said her government had invested “Rs300bn in the Apni Chhat Apna Ghar initiative, Rs200bn in Green Buses [..] we are building the world’s biggest cancer hospital”. “What have you done?” the chief minister asked. Taking note of the scrutiny around her daughter’s graduation ceremony, she insisted that she had borne the expenses, with the total bill amounting to Rs27.5 million. “A chief minister or prime minister is never on leave, and none of their visits is personal. I am working while I am on the plane. I work wherever I am,” CM Maryam claimed. She further contended that, given the nature of her role, she could not afford to lose contact with her government at any time. “If I lose contact with my government on an eight-hour flight and if there is an issue, who is going to handle it?” she asked. Addressing the gathering, CM Maryam held up a “receipt” of the expenses on her phone. CM Maryam said she did not owe “these vloggers and YouTubers a justification”; however, she maintained, “I would still present an explanation in the court of the public.” She said that when her tenure ends, “I will not be taking this plane home with me”; however, the chief minister maintained that her trips to Brazil, Japan, China or Türkiye were undertaken “so I could showcase my government’s progress.” “So, yes, I hope that I get to go again on the plane,” she said. CM Maryam recalled that the day she was set to return to Pakistan, several commercial flights were cancelled due to an issue with the United Kingdom’s air traffic control system. “People travelling by commercial flights had to extend their stay by five to six days, and if I did not have the plane, I would have been stuck and lost five to six days. That is not just five to six days for Maryam Nawaz but five to six projects for the people of Punjab,” she said. “I don’t have time to waste,” CM Maryam said, claiming that she often worked till midnight. “I then wake up at 8am and come back to work. Every waking moment, my office is with me, whether I am in Murree or London.” In response to the criticism, she further said, “Kids, keep at it; may God give you more success in your business. I don’t owe you an answer; I am answerable only to the people.” The chief minister also took a jibe at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi over his recent visit to Lahore, without naming him. “As you saw, some people from KP came to Punjab; he was sitting on the roadside, but no one barely recognised the individual,” CM Maryam remarked. She noted that the visit was “so unsuccessful” that she had to “scold” her deputy commissioners “for not being able to scrounge up at least 400-500 people for a welcome, but even they could not find anyone willing to come”. CM Maryam said that the “individual from KP” was making statements questioning the government’s legitimacy. However, he failed to get people’s attention, she added. “Instead, he sat in a police vehicle forcibly and attempted to stage an abduction. He thought perhaps the act would create some drama,” in reference to the KP CM’s claim that he was “abducted” by authorities in Lahore and later “thrown” by the roadside. Punjab government has denied the allegation.

Pakistan ranked among bottom three in WEF's Global Gender Gap Report 2026. Pakistan ranked third-to-last in the World Economic Forum’s (WEF) Global Gender Gap Report 2026, with 59.5 per cent gender parity, up almost 3pc from last year . The annual report benchmarked the current state and evolution of gender parity across four key dimensions: economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment. Pakistan scored the lowest out of the 38 lower-middle-income economies, as well as the seven South Asian countries, included in the report. “While Pakistan remains among the lowest-ranked economies in the index, it has nonetheless narrowed its gender gap over time by 5.2 percentage points, up from 54.3pc in 2006,” the report said. “Furthermore, the 2026 edition marks its strongest year-on-year improvement in a decade, driven primarily by substantial gains in educational attainment.” Economic participation and opportunity Pakistan ranked 144th in economic participation and opportunity in 2026, moving up three places from its 147th rank in the same index in 2025. The report revealed that 81.46pc of men participated in the labour force, compared to only 28.21pc of women. According to the report, an overwhelming 93.87pc of legislators, senior officials and managers in Pakistan’s workforce were men, compared to women making up 6.13pc. For the professional and technical workers category, the gap was lower with 30.96pc of the positions being occupied by women. The country ranked 115th in wage equality for similar work and 140th in estimated earned income. The report also revealed that 4.9pc of firms in Pakistan had a female majority ownership, while only 3.4pc firms had female top managers. Educational attainment Pakistan ranked 130th in educational attainment, marking a substantial gain in the category. Male literacy rate in the country was reported to be at 69.14pc, while female literacy rate stood at 48.52pc. Boys’ enrolment in primary education was at 83.01pc compared to 81.08pc among girls. In secondary education, male enrolment stood at 49.99pc, compared to 46.48pc in female enrolment. Pakistan ranked first in the world for enrolment in tertiary education, marking high parity, as 10.71pc of women and 11.01pc of men were enrolled. Health and survival The country ranked 127th in the health and survival category. Within the category, Pakistan ranked first in sex ratio at birth, showing high parity between male and female births. Male healthy life expectancy stood at 57.1pc, compared to 56.69pc for women. Political empowerment Pakistan ranked 107th globally in the political empowerment index. According to the report, 78.31pc of parliamentarians were men, compared to 21.69pc being women. Further, an overwhelming 96.55pc of individuals in ministerial positions were men, compared to only 3.45pc of positions being occupied by women. With a female head of state having ruled the country for 4.73 of the last 50 years, Pakistan ranked 39th in this subindex. Access to finance, justice The report also revealed that women in Pakistan didn’t enjoy equal rights regarding inheritance for widows and daughters. It added that women had “near-equal rights” when it came to access to financial services, land assets and non-land assets. According to the report, women had “restricted rights” when it came to access to justice, while they had “equal rights” for freedom of movement. The report also said that women in Pakistan had “unequal rights” for right to divorce. It added that 24.9pc of women had experienced gendered violence in their lives, and that women in Pakistan had “restricted rights” regarding their reproductive autonomy.

Two siblings’ bodies recovered in Mirpur canal, search for third child called off. JHELUM: The bodies of two siblings, who were allegedly thrown into a canal by their father in Mirpur, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, were recovered on Thursday, while the rescue operation for the third child was abandoned without recovering his body, a rescue official said. Mirpur District Emergency Officer (DEO) Sardar Najam Sadozai said that Rescue-1122 divers were conducting an operation to recover the third child’s body from the Khari Sharif canal in Mirpur. However, in a later update, he confirmed that rescue officials had stopped the operation without recovering the third child’s body. The Khari Sharif canal originates from the Jhelum River and is located in the border area between AJK’s Mirpur and the Mangla Dam canal in Punjab’s Jhelum district. Jhelum District Police Officer (DPO) Shafiq Chaudhry confirmed that police had arrested a man, for allegedly throwing his three children — two daughters and a son — into a canal in Mirpur. According to preliminary investigations, the suspect was allegedly an addict and had an estranged relationship with his wife, who had been living at her paternal home. Further investigation was underway, DPO Chaudhry said. “Police in Jhelum are investigating the suspect from all possible angles to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the disappearance of the children,” he added. The suspect confessed to the crime after his wife raised an alarm over the disappearance of their three children, the senior police official added. According to DPO Chaudhry, the suspect had taken his three children with him “for an outing” but did not return. “As the suspect is also an addict, his wife became alarmed when the children did not return and informed the police,” he said. “The Mangla police station in Jhelum district, taking notice of the complaint, took the man into custody, where he told police that he had thrown his three children into a canal of the Jhelum River,” the senior official said. The police registered a first information report (FIR) on the complaint of the children’s mother under Section 363 of the Pakistan Penal Code. “On September 15, 2026, at around 6pm, I, along with my brother, took the children to Pir Bhechan Darbar for a visit. On our return, my brother stopped the vehicle in front of a bakery on Mangla Road in Dina, and I went to buy some items for the children. “While I was inside the bakery, my husband, Zeeshan, accompanied by two unidentified individuals, approached my brother’s vehicle in my absence and told him: ‘I am going to the City Housing Society; I will take the children with me to the park and return them to you afterwards.’ “Persuaded by his words, my brother handed all three children over to Zeeshan. Shortly afterwards, both my brother and I became deeply concerned.” The complainant added that when she tried to contact the suspect on his mobile phone, it was switched off. She further said that she and her brother then searched for the children to the best of their ability but were unable to find them.

Pakistan Bar Council urges govt to contain fuel price inflation, provide relief to citizens. ISLAMABAD: A joint meeting of the Executive Committee and Rules Committee of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) on Thursday strongly condemned the unprecedented daily increases in fuel prices, demanding that the government take measures to control the increases and provide relief to citizens. The participants said the daily increases had aggravated inflation and made the cost of living unbearable for ordinary people, particularly those from the middle and lower-middle classes. The joint meeting, presided over by PBC Vice Chairman Pir Muhammad Masood Chishti and PBC Executive Committee Chairman Munir Ahmed Malik, expressed concern in a resolution that the daily increases in fuel prices had caused widespread frustration and unrest among the public and adversely affected people’s purchasing power. The meeting demanded that the government immediately withdraw unnecessary privileges, excessive packages, free fuel facilities, the unnecessary use of official vehicles and other undue expenditures being enjoyed by ministers, government officials and other privileged persons. “The government must take concrete and immediate measures to control fuel price inflation and provide relief to ordinary citizens,” the resolution said. The meeting emphasised that the proposal for a “smart lockdown” was not a solution to the prevailing economic crisis. “Such measures, if imposed, would further burden ordinary citizens, daily-wage earners and businesses.” The PBC called upon the government to take practical steps aimed at facilitating and providing relief to citizens. On Sunday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had announced a “relief scheme” for owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc. Under the scheme, owners of two- and three-wheeled vehicles will receive a subsidy of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while those owning vehicles of up to 800cc will receive the same subsidy on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

Pakistan abstains in UN vote on Iran sanctions panel. UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan abstained on Thursday when the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) voted on a US-sponsored resolution to extend the mandate of the Panel of Experts assisting the council’s Iran sanctions committee. The resolution was rejected after China and Russia, two of the Security Council’s five permanent members, voted against it, effectively vetoing the measure. Eleven of the 15 Council members, including the United States, Britain and France, voted in favour, while two, including Pakistan, abstained. The negotiations on the draft resolution reflected the deep divisions within the council over the Iran nuclear issue, particularly the dispute over the triggering of the “ snapback ” mechanism to reimpose UN sanctions on Iran that had been suspended under the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) and Security Council Resolution 2231 of 2015. China and Russia reiterated their longstanding opposition to the legal and procedural validity of the snapback mechanism. Both permanent members were expected to vote against the draft, which would block its adoption even if it secured nine or more votes in favour. Pakistan’s abstention was explained by its permanent representative, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, who said Islamabad remained concerned that the Iran nuclear issue had become increasingly complicated and that the council had moved away from the spirit of cooperation and peaceful settlement that had accompanied the adoption of Resolution 2231 in 2015. “Diplomacy and dialogue remain the guiding principle” for resolving outstanding issues concerning Iran’s nuclear programme, Ambassador Ahmad told the council. The US draft extends the experts’ mandate until September 2027 and asks the panel to provide recommendations on updating sanctions-related measures, quarterly reports on its work and an annual report to the UNSC. The panel, established under UNSC Resolution 1929 of 2010, monitors implementation of measures imposed on Iran and provides the council with assessments and recommendations. Its mandate was due to expire on Sept 26. The dispute over the panel is part of a wider disagreement over the status of the UN sanctions regime following the invocation of the snapback mechanism by Britain, France and Germany in 2025. Pakistan has consistently argued that the nuclear issue should be resolved through negotiations rather than confrontation. In his statement on Thursday, Ambassador Ahmad recalled that Pakistan had urged the council last year to provide additional time for diplomacy through a technical extension of Resolution 2231. He said Islamabad had warned that a non-confrontational and cooperative approach would have provided greater space for a lasting settlement. “The Iran nuclear issue should be addressed through peaceful means,” he said, stressing that the rights, obligations and responsibilities of the parties concerned must be respected. Pakistan also reaffirmed its support for the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), describing it as the technical body responsible for implementing safeguards agreements. “The IAEA should ensure this important work as per its mandate, independently and without political interference,” Ambassador Ahmad said. He called for renewed diplomatic engagement and urged the parties to return to negotiations. Pakistan also referred to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding , calling on the parties to implement their commitments under the agreement and return to the negotiating table.

Pakistan, China reaffirm consensus at inaugural Boundary Joint Commission meeting. The inaugural meeting of the Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission (BJC) concluded in Islamabad on Thursday, with both sides reaffirming their consensus and agreeing on a framework for future cooperation under the commission. According to the Foreign Office (FO), the meeting was held in Islamabad on Sept 16 and 17, marking the formal launch of the commission. The BJC was envisaged under the 2013 China-Pakistan Agreement on the Boundary Management System. “Both sides described the establishment of the commission as a vital milestone in further strengthening the Pakistan-China All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership,” the FO said. According to the statement, discussions at the inaugural meeting covered a wide range of matters related to border management and cooperation, including cross-border coordination, the movement of goods and people, joint border surveys and people-to-people linkages. The meeting concluded with the signing of the minutes, reaffirming the two sides’ consensus and setting out a framework for future cooperation under the commission, the statement said. “Both sides agreed to hold the next meeting of the commission in China on mutually convenient dates,” the FO said. The Pakistan delegation was led by Bilal Mahmood Chaudhary, Director General (China) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while the Chinese delegation was led by Li Ya, Deputy Director General of the Department of Boundary and Ocean Affairs at China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Other representatives from the ministries of foreign affairs, defence, interior, commerce and communications, as well as customs, survey and other boundary management authorities, also attended the meeting. The commission has its origins in the 2013 Agreement on the Boundary Management System , signed during the visit of then Chinese Premier Li Keqiang to Islamabad. Article 45 of the agreement provides for the establishment of the joint commission to oversee the implementation of border management arrangements. The mechanism will provide an institutional framework for dealing with practical issues along the border, including the maintenance and inspection of the boundary, joint surveys, boundary marker issues, the management of cross-border facilities and the handling of incidents involving the border. Its activation also gives the two countries a mechanism for regular coordination on a border that is important for movement between Pakistan and China, including thr­ough the Khunjerab crossing, and for trade and connectivity linked to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

Punjab Assembly begins evaluation of AI use in public services. LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly has begun parliamentary evaluation of artificial intelligence and digital governance, with its Special Committee No. 13 examining the use of AI in public services and the safeguards needed to protect citizens’ rights. Chaired by Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan, the committee held its inaugural meeting on Thursday. It is the first parliamentary committee in Pakistan and the South Asian region with a dedicated mandate covering artificial intelligence and digital governance. The meeting followed a three-day workshop for committee members, held in Islamabad from Sept 2 to 4 by UNDP Pakistan and the United Kingdom’s international development organisation. The workshop examined artificial intelligence and digital technologies, their potential benefits and risks, and the principles of responsible governance. The committee considered an initial programme of parliamentary inquiry into the use of AI in Punjab, focusing on transparency, accountability, citizens’ rights, data security, effective remedies and meaningful human oversight. Two provincial public service systems were identified for initial examination. The first is the Punjab Safe Cities Authority’s AI-assisted e-challan system . The committee will examine the accuracy of violation detection, human validation of violations, citizens’ access to evidence, mechanisms for challenging and reviewing decisions, and the handling of related data. The second relates to welfare assistance linked to the Punjab Socio-Economic Registry (PSER). The committee will examine registration and accessibility, data accuracy, eligibility assessments, explanations for adverse decisions, correction of inaccurate information and opportunities for reconsideration. Importantly, the committee said it would establish through evidence how eligibility was actually determined — whether through manual assessment, fixed rules, statistical scoring, machine learning or a combination of these methods — rather than assuming that AI was involved. The committee also discussed the constitutional and legal implications of emerging digital technologies, including digital harms, deepfakes, threats to democratic trust, risks to women and vulnerable groups, data governance and institutional capacity.

PM’s fuel subsidy scheme faces first-day hurdles at petrol pumps. ISLAMABAD: The much-touted fuel subsidy scheme launched by the prime minister faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app, claiming they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less. After receiving several complaints in this regard, Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima visited various fuel stations in Rawalpindi to ensure that subsidised petrol was available to registered consumers. A day earlier, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) expressed concerns that its members were unaware of the subsidy disbursement mechanism and feared they would have to run from pillar to post to recover the amount. However, to resolve the matter, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, along with officials from the relevant ministries, held a meeting with the PPDA on Thursday to discuss the mechanism for implementing the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme. PPDA Chairman Malik Khuda Baksh led the delegation, which joined the meeting via video link. The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) briefed the participants on the reimbursement mechanism and assured them that claims submitted under the scheme would be processed within 48 hours, ensuring timely payments to participating petroleum dealers. The Ministry of IT and Telecommunications briefed the participants on the digital system developed to implement the scheme. The meeting was also informed that a dedicated control room had been established to assist petrol pumps and address their queries and complaints. Petrol pumps can contact the control room at 9772 for assistance. The meeting was further informed that funds for three months had been earmarked for the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme, with Rs25 billion for the first month already provided to SBP to facilitate timely reimbursement under the scheme. The PPDA chairman said the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme was welcomed by petroleum dealers, but a lack of information about the disbursement of subsidy amounts was creating confusion among its members. “We assure you that all our members across the country will support the PM’s fuel relief scheme,” Khuda Baksh said. During the meeting, the petroleum minister appreciated the cooperation extended by petroleum dealers and emphasised the importance of close coordination among all stakeholders for the effective, transparent and timely implementation of the relief initiative. OCAC warns of disruption In another development, the Oil Companies Advisory Committee (OCAC) warned the government of disruption to the oil supply chain if Rs67 billion in price differential claims (PDC) pending since March 2026 were not settled. In a letter to the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) chairman, the OCAC claimed that the pending PDC amount was equivalent to five imported cargoes of petrol. The letter, written by OCAC Secretary General Dr Nazir Abbas Zaidi, was forwarded to the petroleum minister and the Petroleum Division secretary. It said oil companies were now unable to finance an uninterrupted fuel supply chain due to Rs66.7 billion in outstanding PDCs. The OCAC said the situation had been further aggravated by the evolving geopolitical environment and potential disruptions to regional supply routes, including the East-West Pipeline. The oil companies warned that the country could face significant supply-side challenges under the current regional scenario, while the oil industry’s liquidity continued to deplete due to a lack of support from the authorities. “Any resulting supply-chain disruption must not be on account of the oil industry,” the OCAC said in the letter. Despite repeated communications and extensive verification and audit processes, the OCAC had requested settlement by June 8, 2026, but the matter remained unresolved, it added. “We urge Ogra to urgently conclude the verification process and release all verified and approved claims, including the approved premium differential claims relating to Motor Spirit (petrol) imports during the recent geopolitical crisis, referring to the situation arising following the US-Israeli attack on Iran at the end of February 2026.” The OCAC said oil marketing companies (OMCs) had consistently supported the government, particularly when fuel security and uninterrupted supplies were at stake. “Yet today, the same industry is facing an acute and worsening liquidity crisis and effectively being required to finance the supply chain while its own liquidity is being progressively drained,” the OCAC said, inviting government functionaries to meet its members at its head office in Karachi. The OCAC also reminded the government of the need to revise OMC margins, adding that they were last revised in September 2023 and had remained unchanged despite significant increases in operating, financing, technology, regulatory and compliance costs. The letter added that dealer margins were increased by Rs1.34 per litre in August 2026, while the approved Rs1.22 per litre increase in OMC margins remained to be notified and implemented. “Unlike dealers, OMCs carry the full responsibility for product procurement, import financing, inventory management, logistics and ensuring product availability across the country, in addition to meeting ever-expanding regulatory and digitisation requirements, with implementation timelines being progressively compressed,” the letter said. It demanded immediate notification and implementation of the Rs1.22 per litre increase in OMC margins and the establishment of a predictable mechanism for periodic margin revisions.

PM Shehbaz reaches London before heading to New York for UNGA session. ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday reached London for a two-day stopover before proceeding to the United States to attend the high-level segment of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. According to a source in the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier would proceed to the US on Saturday to attend the UNGA session. The source said the prime minister was likely to return to the country on Sept 27 or 28 after attending the UNGA session and would again stop over in London for a day or two. “In fact, travelling from Pakistan to the US is quite a long journey, therefore, PM Shehbaz opted to stay somewhere, preferably in London,” the source added. According to the Foreign Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly on Sept 25. “On the sidelines of the UN session, he is expected to hold bilateral meetings with world leaders and participate in high-level events,” the FO said. The prime minister will be accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, federal ministers and senior government officials during the New York leg of the visit. “The premier will present Pakistan’s perspective on regional and global developments and highlight the country’s priorities at the UNGA,” it said. The official theme of the 81st session is ‘Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All’, and the UNGA debate is expected to run from Sept 22 to 26, with a final sitting on Sept 28. However, ongoing fighting between Washington and Tehran is expected to feature prominently in discussions among world leaders, particularly over the security of the Strait of Hormuz, regional stability and the possibility of finding a diplomatic way out of the confrontation. The premier is expected to highlight Pakistan’s efforts to find a peaceful solution to the ongoing US-Iran war.

10 terrorists killed in KP ops: ISPR. ISLAMABAD: Security forces killed 10 terrorists in separate operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa between Sept 15 and 17, while six soldiers were martyred in an improvised explosive device (IED) blast, the military’s media wing said on Thursday. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), an intelligence-based operation was carried out in North Waziristan after reports of the presence of terrorists in the area. Security forces effectively targeted their hideout, killing six khwarij belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al-Khawarij in an intense exchange of fire. The state uses the term Fitna al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). In another clash in Hangu, four terrorists were killed. Military’s media wing says six soldiers martyred in IED blast On Sept 17, an IED struck a security forces convoy, resulting in the martyrdom of six soldiers, according to the ISPR. Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the terrorists killed in the operations, the ISPR stated. It added that the slain men were involved in several terrorist activities in these areas. Awaran operation Separately, security for­ces killed three terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in the Badrang area of Balo­chistan’s Awaran district. A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the possession of the terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan , according to security sources. Fitna al Hindustan is a term designated by the state for terrorist organisations in Balochistan. Published in Dawn, September 18th, 2026

US approves sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia. WASHINGTON: The United States has approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth warplanes to Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Thursday, the latest major arms purchase by Riyadh since the start of the Iran war. Saudi Arabia has long sought to buy F-35s, but officials from Israel — currently the only country in the Middle East to operate the jets — have voiced concern about their sale to Riyadh despite a push by the Saudis to normalise relations. “The proposed sale will improve Saudi Arabia’s capability to deter current and future threats by strengthening its homeland defence, and improving interoperability with US forces,” the State Department said in a statement. “It will also augment Saudi Arabia’s operational aircraft and enhance its air-to-air, and air-to-ground self-defence capability,” the statement said. The State Department has notified Congress about the proposed sale, which would require the approval of US lawmakers. It did not provide a time frame for the delivery of the jets. The F-35 sale “will not alter the military balance in the region,” the State Department said, in keeping with longstanding US policy that Israel must have a military edge over potential regional adversaries. The United States has so far only allowed the sales of F-35s to its closest allies, including a number of European Nato allies and Israel. Washington kicked Nato member Turkiye out of the F-35 programme in 2019 because Ankara’s purchase of a Russian air defence system sparked fears that Moscow could acquire the plane’s technology. Published in Dawn, September 18th, 2026

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs390.79 per litre while HSD will cost Rs424.92 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 18 (Friday). According to Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the increase is primarily linked to higher petrol and diesel prices in the international market. The regulator said the prices were revised based on international market rates, premiums and other relevant factors. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices, including requiring markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres. On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Imaan, Hadi sent on judicial remand in another case after SC suspends sentences. ISLAMABAD: Hours after the Supreme Court suspended the sentences of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) rejected police’s request for a 30-day physical remand of the couple and sent them to jail on judicial remand. On January 24, an Islamabad sessions court sentenced Imaan and Hadi to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). The convictions of the couple, who had already been jailed the day before in a separate case, were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . Islamabad ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain passed the order after the two accused were produced before the court for a hearing in a case registered against them at Kohsar police station. Soon after their release, Islamabad police personnel, led by the SSP Operations, reached Adiala jail and arrested the two again in connection with the case. The police subsequently produced them before the ATC late at night. Former federal minister Shireen Mazari confirmed the development, saying attempts were being made to keep the couple in jail. Speaking to Dawn , Imaan’s counsel Riasat Ali Azad also confirmed the development, saying a large contingent of Islamabad police had shifted the couple to Kohsar police station. The case at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station was registered on March 22, 2025, on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio. Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added. The FIR included Section 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), Section 341 (wrongful restraint), Section 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), Section 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and Section 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties). SC suspends sentences Earlier today, the apex court suspended the couple’s sentences in the controversial social media posts case after a two-judge SC bench, headed by Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, took up the couple’s appeals against the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) refusal in February to suspend the sentences. On Thursday, the SC granted the couple bail against surety bonds of Rs200,000 and ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict. “Both are lawyers and we are keeping their honour,” observed Justice Afghan, but also asked senior counsel Faisal Siddiqui, the couple’s lawyer, to tell the appellants to observe the court’s decorum. “There is a difference between a lawyer and an ordinary person,” the judge observed. According to a written order, the SC converted the petitions of both Imaan and Hadi into appeals and suspended the operation of the January 24 conviction. The court also ordered the release of petitioners — noting they were practising advocates — on bail till the decision of their pending appeals before IHC. The release was subject to furnishing personal surety bonds worth Rs200,000 for each with the SC’s additional registrar (judicial). The SC will issue a detailed verdict on the case later. Earlier, the SC had repeatedly adjourned hearings in the case on the grounds that the IHC had fixed their application for suspension of sentence along with the main appeal. During Thursday’s hearing, Siddiqui argued that the SC had issued its first order on May 12 in which the IHC was asked to decide the applicants’ petition for suspension of sentence as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of two weeks. On May 12, the SC ordered the IHC to decide Imaan and Hadi’s sentence suspension pleas within two weeks. Despite the May 26 deadline having already passed, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) challenged the SC order and sought its withdrawal. During the proceedings, Siddiqui also read out the order sheets from various IHC hearings. At one point, the SC directed Additional Attorney General (AAG) Rana Asadullah Khan, who was standing at the rostrum, to take a seat, adding that the court will hear Siddiqui first. “Let him sit, though he has certainly worn us out,” Siddiqui quipped and cited former chief justice Asif Saeed Khosa’s remarks that a case would only be adjourned upon the death of a judge or a lawyer. The counsel regretted that the IHC adjourned the case multiple times and that his clients’ request for an early hearing was rejected by the high court’s registrar office. “What transpired at the high court came as a surprise to us,” the counsel said. “These days are an era of surprises,” remarked Justice Ibrahim. During the hearing, the AAG contended that the IHC has not yet issued any adverse ruling, adding that seven opportunities were provided in the trial court. He highlighted that the judicial forum for the suspension of a sentence under Section 426 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) was the high court. Justice Afghan observed that the IHC always cited the SC directives for early disposal of the case but does not act upon them. The judge also asked AAG Khan whether he would give any assurance that proceedings would be held at the next IHC hearing, to which the latter replied that he cannot represent any high court judge in the SC. Later, the SC suspended the sentence of the applicants and ordered their release on bail, pending the IHC’s final verdict. In their applications, the applicants had stated that it was a settled policy of the SC that criminal matters have to be given priority, especially when the matters pertain to bail or suspension of sentence. Moreover, in Section 7 of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023, it was expressly stated that any application pleading urgency shall be fixed for hearing within a period of 14 days. The application contended that Imaan was a young female lawyer and has remained incarcerated for a long period of time in a case where conviction was the “result of a sham trial”. The case Imaan and Hadi have been in jail since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association (IHCBA) president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court convicted Imaan and Hadi in the social media posts case. It sentenced the duo to 10 years’ imprisonment under Section 10 (cyber terrorism), five years’ imprisonment under Section 9 (glorification of an offence) and two years’ imprisonment under Section 26-A (false and fake information) of Peca. All sentences were to run concurrently. The case stemmed from a complaint filed on Aug 12, 2025 by the assistant director (investigating officer) at the NCCIA Islamabad, before the Federal Investigation Agency’s Cybercrime Reporting Centre. The complaint accused Imaan of disseminating and “propagating narratives that align with hostile terrorist groups and proscribed organisations”, while her husband was implicated for reposting some of her posts. The first information report (FIR) in the case alleged that the two held security forces responsible for cases of missing persons in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. It also stated that they had portrayed the armed forces as ineffective against proscribed groups, including the banned outfits Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). Judge Majoka had indicted Imaan and Hadi in the case on Oct 30, 2025 and issued arrest warrants for the couple on Nov 5, 2025. The judge then reissued arrest warrants for them in January after repeated non-appearances. After being convicted, the couple challenged the sentences by filing separate appeals in the IHC on February 7. Taking up those appeals and sentence suspension pleas on February 19, the IHC issued notices to the respondents but refused to suspend the sentences. On April 30, Imaan and Hadi moved a separate appeal before the SC against the IHC’s February order. They sought an early hearing of the plea in June, after which notices were issued on July 6. After the SC’s intervention , the IHC finally declared the jailed couple’s pleas seeking suspension of sentences as admissible on July 25. Days later, Imaan moved the SC again seeking an early hearing of the challenge against the IHC order. Additional input by Mohammad Asghar

Court vs court. A SUPREME Court order directing the hospitalisation of former prime minister Imran Khan for medical tests and treatment has now turned into a much bigger crisis than anyone anticipated. After the court’s original order was disregarded by the government , like so many others before it, the matter landed before the Federal Constitutional Court via a separate case filed by three other Adiala inmates seeking similar treatment. The FCC has since taken control of the Imran Khan hospitalisation case as well, much to the SC’s chagrin . To observers, the FCC’s move directly challenges a May ruling issued by Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi, in which he had described the SC and FCC as “coordinate courts exercising clearly demarcated jurisdictions over distinct matters”. However, the current dispute underlines a clear jurisdictional collision between the two courts, which still seem rather uncertain regarding what each is supposed to be doing since the 27th Amendment . At the heart of the crisis is the 27th Amendment, which had substantially rearranged constitutional jurisdiction by creating a completely new judicial forum, the FCC, and placing major constitutional questions and fundamental rights matters within its domain. The FCC invoked that same jurisdiction days ago to summon the complete records of cases concerning Mr Khan’s hospital transfer from the SC, indicating that it intended to frame the matter as a question of determining whether prisoners are constitutionally entitled to such treatment. However, it then went a step further and also fixed the case before itself. To its credit, the SC has responded with restraint. The three-member bench hearing the case merely remarked that the FCC’s order had raised “considerable legal and constitutional significance” and then adjourned for three weeks while seeking comment from the attorney general over whether the FCC’s order was, indeed, binding on the SC. Mr Khan’s hospitalisation, of course, seems moot at this point. Perhaps matters were bound to arrive at this juncture thanks to the undue haste with which the 27th Amendment was foisted upon the nation. It appears that its text never settled the matter of what happens when a constitutional question arises in an ongoing SC case, especially when such a case pertains to the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Contempt of Court Ordinance, which are very much within the SC’s remit. It is even more remarkable that a crisis of this nature has erupted at the highest level of the judiciary over what was otherwise a rather straightforward order to transfer an ailing prisoner to a hospital and get them the treatment required. It is certainly not a good look for the current dispensation that the fragility of the architecture that props it up keeps being exposed, and over matters that ought to be minor in perspective.
